A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same CKA-RL research work, with complete main text, Appendices A–G, and the checklist. Text, equations, tables, and rendered figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CKA-RL evaluations on Meta-World, SpaceInvaders, and Freeway, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, efficiency measurements, and knowledge-vector analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendices E–F, including numerical comparisons and experimental plots.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same frozen base model, task-specific knowledge vectors, learned adaptation weights, and cosine-similarity-based vector merging. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Meta-World sequence of ten tasks repeated twice, ten SpaceInvaders modes, and eight Freeway modes. Section 5 and Appendix C contain no coverage changes.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Baseline, FT-1, FT-N, ProgNet, PackNet, MaskNet, CReLUs, CompoNet, and CbpNet. Comparator membership in the final-policy, forgetting, and efficiency comparisons also remains unchanged; citation numbers alone change.

E3.justification: The SAC/PPO training procedures, one-million-step task budgets, architectures, hyperparameters, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. The final-policy and forgetting evaluation procedures are also identical.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the component ablation, knowledge-pool-size sensitivity study, convergence comparison, final-policy and forgetting analyses, efficiency studies, and Appendix F cosine-similarity analysis without revisions.

E5.justification: Both report experiments using ten random seeds and retain the same uncertainty entries in Table 1 and shaded curves. No run-count disclosure, uncertainty procedure, or significance test is added or changed.

E6.justification: The numerical entries, plotted results, and reported findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains CKA-RL's average performance of 0.7498 and forward transfer of 0.5049, while Table 3 retains final-policy performance of 0.3966.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, mathematical definitions, and Equations (1)–(17) are unchanged. Appendix A retains the same three lemmas and three corollaries concerning drift, interference, and merging stability.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same knowledge-adaptation and merging contributions, scalability claims, and reported improvements of 4.20% in performance and 8.02% in forward transfer.

C2.justification: Interpretations of knowledge reuse, orthogonality, forgetting, and efficiency are unchanged. Appendix G retains the same limitations concerning unverified performance in complex real-world environments and larger architectures.

D1.justification: Section 5.1, Appendix D, and Tables 5–6 provide identical implementation and hyperparameter information. The source-code access statement and repository address are also unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix B retains its GRPO and DAPO discussion but changes the cited sources. v1's Zhang et al. 'Group relative policy optimization' and Chen et al. 'Decoupled clip and dynamic sampling policy optimization' entries are replaced by Shao et al.'s DeepSeekMath and Yu et al.'s DAPO entries in v2. This is a limited source-attribution revision; the broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: Editorial changes are limited to the two rewritten reference entries, associated citation renumbering, and the arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific prose, terminology, and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The bibliography reflows, including changed spacing and movement of the Meta-World, RECALL, and IQ references from page 13 to page 14. All eleven figures and seven tables retain their displays and placement, apart from citation-number updates.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information are unchanged. The GRPO/DAPO source replacements could improve attribution, but the supplied PDFs do not establish whether the replacement references correct the earlier entries. Their bibliographic accuracy therefore leaves the direction of any overall quality change uncertain.
